category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: X-Detect: Explainable Adversarial Patch Detection for Object Detectors in Retail
key_idea: Patch detector for object detectors that runs explainable-by-design checks (object extraction, scene manipulation, feature transformation) on each scene, raising real-time alerts that come with explanations and cover unfamiliar attacks.
method: Ensemble of explainable-by-design base detectors whose outputs decide whether an alert is raised; an explanation is attached to each alert.
data: COCO; the authors' Superstore dataset; physical smart-shopping-cart setup with 17 patch attacks in 1,700 adversarial videos (abstract).
reported_result: Abstract (Crossref record): beats compared methods at separating benign from adversarial scenes in all five attack scenarios, adaptive attacks included, at a 0% false positive rate, with actionable explanations.
relation_to_project: Named baseline on slide 01 and the closest prior work for contribution 6 (explain the alarm): explanation by design, not post-hoc heat maps. Retail scenes, not road signs; what the operator sees is not described in the abstract.
notes: Journal version of arXiv 2306.08422 (2023 preprint). Abstract mentions a demo; location not seen. Also catalogued by LIT_A1 (P2-P134); coordinator to deduplicate.

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: PhySense: Defending Physically Realizable Attacks for Autonomous Systems via Consistency Reasoning
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS 2024)
key_idea: Cross-checks perception labels against physical object evidence (3D size, texture, motion behaviour, interactions with other road users) in a CRF over a spatial-temporal graph to detect and correct attack-induced misclassifications in real time.
method: 2D detections lifted to a 3D kinematic model; texture and size attributes, attention-BiLSTM behaviour recognition and rule-based interaction checks fused by CRF inference; parallel, pipelined execution.
data: nuScenes, KITTI and a custom CARLA set with patch and projection attacks; 8.6 hours of real driving with a Tesla Model 3 (authors' project page).
reported_result: Authors' project page and paper table: over 99% detection accuracy and about 98% correction accuracy across datasets; VehicleSec 2025 poster: about 0.037 s average run time per frame.
relation_to_project: Closest prior work to the shared slide pipeline (detector output checked against independent physical evidence); its alarm reason is a violated physical property, not a heat map. Needs 3D lifting and tracking, heavier than the cheap cues of slides 01 to 05.
code_or_data: https://sites.google.com/view/physense (project page states code and datasets are released) UNVERIFIED
notes: Crossref record carries no abstract; abstract and a results table read on the authors' pages through websearch. Author page lists ACM artifact badges. Also catalogued by LIT_A5 (P2-P513); coordinator to deduplicate.

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: SentiNet: Detecting Localized Universal Attacks Against Deep Learning Systems
key_idea: Extracts highly salient contiguous regions with interpretability and object-detection techniques, overlays each on many held-out clean images, and flags regions that keep causing misclassification as localized universal attacks.
method: Saliency-based region extraction, overlay test on held-out clean images, decision on how often the overlay flips predictions.
reported_result: Abstract (IEEE page): malicious regions cause misclassifications on held-out images far more often than benign salient regions; no numbers read.
relation_to_project: Origin of region-level alarm evidence (the disputed region) used on slide 01; classifier setting and many extra forward passes per input clash with the lightweight goal. SLAP (LIT_A3, LIT_A4) reports bypassing it with projected light.
notes: arXiv 1812.00292 is the 2018 preprint. A patch survey (arXiv 2206.08304, not catalogued) notes that random overlay placement can occlude the main object and yield false region proposals. Also in LIT_A1 (P2-P135) and LIT_A3 (P2-P340).

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: Knowledge Enhanced Machine Learning Pipeline against Diverse Adversarial Attacks
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2021), PMLR 139
key_idea: Links a sign classifier to weak auxiliary detectors (border shape, colour, content) through permissive and preventive first-order logic rules in a factor graph, so evidence that contradicts domain knowledge overrides attacked predictions.
method: Weighted factor graph over main-model and auxiliary-model outputs; statistical inference for the final label; sufficient conditions for a robustness gain proved.
data: GTSRB 12-class subset with 12 permissive and 12 preventive rules (arXiv full-text snippet); LISA named on the ICML slides.
reported_result: PMLR abstract: higher robustness than adversarial training and other baselines against physical, Lp-bounded and unforeseen attacks and natural corruptions, white-box and black-box, with high clean accuracy; no numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Rule-based monitor for slide 01 (class implies shape, colour, content): a violated rule is a readable alarm reason. Needs per-class hand-written rules and auxiliary models; corrects labels rather than raising a calibrated alarm with abstain.
notes: Verified against the arXiv API record; ICML 2021 publication read on the PMLR page. VOGUES (USENIX Security 2024 snippet) reports KEMLP at 0% FPR in its comparison. Also in LIT_X12 (P2-P2101).

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: Fast and Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Adversarial Traffic Sign Detection
key_idea: ViLAS flags adversarial road-sign inputs by pairing the image with class-label text in a small custom vision-language model that attaches to any existing sign recognizer.
method: Custom fast vision-language model scoring image and class-label text; detector placed beside the recognition model.
reported_result: Abstract (Crossref record): average AUC 0.94 against four attacks on four target models versus 0.75 for a generic image-attack detector; 4.4 ms versus 9.3 ms for an off-the-shelf VLM and CLIP.
relation_to_project: Lightweight, sign-specific detection baseline for slide 01 and contribution 5; outputs an alarm score, and the abstract describes no explanation of which visual cue failed.
notes: Abstract calls the target models action recognition models, which looks like an error for sign recognition; check the full text. The abstract novelty claim is not repeated here.

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: Jujutsu: A Two-stage Defense against Adversarial Patch Attacks on Deep Neural Networks
venue: ACM Asia Conference on Computer and Communications Security (AsiaCCS 2023)
key_idea: Detects patches by moving the most salient region of a suspect image into the least-salient area of hold-out images and testing whether the label follows it; then rebuilds that region with GAN inpainting.
method: Saliency-map localisation, guided feature transplantation with a label-consistency test, GAN inpainting for mitigation.
data: ImageNette, ImageNet, CelebA and Place365 (code repository README); physical-world and adaptive attacks (arXiv abstract).
reported_result: arXiv abstract: outperforms four existing defenses across four datasets and 8 models; no rates read in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Region-level evidence plus a consistency test, refining SentiNet to cut false positives; classifier only, and extra forward passes plus inpainting per input weigh against slide 01 latency goals.
notes: arXiv id read on the arXiv abstract page through websearch (not in the ledger; arXiv host stopped). The code repository uses an earlier paper title.

category: X4-F2 Explanation methods for object detectors
title: Black-box Explanation of Object Detectors via Saliency Maps
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2021)
key_idea: Black-box saliency for object detectors: random masks perturb the image, and a similarity metric combining box IoU, class-probability cosine and objectness weights each mask, explaining both localization and class, even for missed objects.
method: RISE-style mask sampling; the detector runs on every masked image; detection-vector similarity weights each mask; the weighted sum is the saliency map.
data: MS-COCO with YOLOv3 and Faster R-CNN; user trust test with YOLOv3 versus YOLOv3-Tiny on Mechanical Turk (paper text).
reported_result: Paper text (CVF open access): on 242 objects, 50.2% versus 27.4% of user answers judged the more accurate detector's explanations better; per-class average maps exposed context use and an inserted bias.
relation_to_project: Model-agnostic way to show which region drove a detection, for the explanation output of slides 01 to 05; ODExAI (arXiv 2504.19249) reports about 98.67 s per explanation, so it suits offline analysis, not per-frame alarms.
notes: Verified against the arXiv API record (2020); CVPR 2021 venue read on the CVF open access page; method and user-study excerpts also read. A third-party implementation exists in the xaitk-saliency library (seen in search results).

category: X4-F2 Explanation methods for object detectors
title: ODAM: Gradient-based instance-specific visual explanations for object detection
key_idea: White-box method that weights intermediate feature maps by the gradients of a single detection's attributes (class score, box coordinates), giving instance-specific heat maps; Odam-Train and Odam-NMS reuse the explanations.
method: Gradient-weighted activation maps per predicted attribute; works for one-stage, two-stage and transformer detectors; a training scheme makes explanations distinct per object.
data: FCOS with FPN among the detectors; crowd scenes for Odam-NMS (paper text).
reported_result: Abstract: higher-quality explanations than the state of the art in effectiveness and efficiency; no numbers read.
relation_to_project: Per-detection heat map from one backward pass, cheaper than sampling, for the slide explanation output; the authors describe D-RISE as computationally intensive and noisy. Still a heat map, not a physical cause.
notes: Verified against the arXiv API record; ICLR 2023 per the ICLR poster page. Journal extension in IEEE TPAMI 2024 (IEEE CSDL page seen, DOI not checked) adds a user-trust and eye-gaze agreement study.

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Methods Explaining Object Detectors
key_idea: Applies model and data randomization sanity checks to gradient saliency maps of three detectors and finds explainability depends more on the detector than on the saliency method; checks should be run per class.
method: Model randomization test scored with qualitative criteria and SSIM; guided backpropagation, integrated gradients and SmoothGrad variants; class and box explanations.
data: COCO test 2017 with Faster R-CNN, SSD512 and EfficientDet-D0; a marine debris detector set (arXiv text).
reported_result: arXiv abstract: EfficientDet-D0 is the most interpretable detector regardless of saliency method and passes the checks with few problems.
relation_to_project: Reusable test that an alarm explanation really depends on the model (contribution 6); explanation quality is tied to the detector, which matters when the detector stays frozen.
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed per the record read; a conference version was not checked. Builds on the sanity checks of Adebayo et al. (NeurIPS 2018).

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: DExT: Detector Explanation Toolkit
key_idea: Toolkit that explains both box and class decisions of SSD512, Faster R-CNN and EfficientDet-D0 with gradient methods, merges multi-object explanations into one view, and ranks methods by insertion, deletion and a user study.
method: Guided backpropagation, integrated gradients and SmoothGrad variants per decision; four multi-object visualisations (PCA, contours, density clustering, convex polygons); insertion and deletion in single-box and realistic settings; user study.
reported_result: arXiv text: SmoothGrad with guided backpropagation gives the most faithful explanations overall; all methods explain SSD more faithfully than the other two detectors.
relation_to_project: Ready-made explanation and evaluation path for a frozen detector (slides 01 to 05, contribution 6); gradient heat maps only, no physical cause.
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed per the record read. Same authors as P2-P1309.

category: X4-F2 Explanation methods for object detectors
title: G-CAME: Gaussian-Class Activation Mapping Explainer for Object Detectors
key_idea: Class-activation-map explainer for object detectors that uses a Gaussian kernel to produce per-detection saliency; a later benchmark reports it localizes best and runs fastest, with diffuse maps.
method: Class activation mapping combined with a Gaussian kernel (title and benchmark description); per-detection saliency.
reported_result: ODExAI preprint (arXiv 2504.19249), YOLOX on MS COCO: highest pointing-game scores (PG 94.31%, EBPG 67.16%) and about 0.43 s per explanation versus 98.67 s for D-RISE; lowest sparsity.
relation_to_project: Fast heat-map option when latency matters (contribution 5); explains the detector, not the attack cause.
notes: Abstract not read in this run (arXiv host stopped); results quoted from the ODExAI preprint, authorship overlap not checked.

category: X4-F2 Explanation methods for object detectors
title: Explaining YOLO: Leveraging Grad-CAM to Explain Object Detections
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop of the Austrian Association for Pattern Recognition (OAGM 2021)
key_idea: Integrates Grad-CAM into YOLO by tracing each kept box back through non-maximum suppression to its objectness and class neurons, giving per-detection attribution maps; normalization strongly changes how maps read.
method: Grad-CAM on the last convolutional layer of the YOLO head for the neurons behind a chosen detection; detection-, image- and dataset-level normalization compared.
reported_result: Paper text: one explanation takes about half a second; the normalization choice decides whether explanations can be compared across images.
relation_to_project: Per-box explanation of a frozen YOLO at modest cost; the authors name run-time detection of false detections from explanations as future work, close to the slide idea.
notes: Verified against the arXiv API record; workshop DOI taken from the arXiv record, not checked in Crossref. Review process of the workshop not checked.

category: X4-F2 Explanation methods for object detectors
title: Fast Explanation Using Shapley Value for Object Detection
key_idea: Trains an explainer network to estimate per-pixel Shapley values for every detected object, so detector saliency maps are produced in real time at test time without sampling.
method: Learned explainer model approximating Shapley values per object (abstract fragment and survey description).
relation_to_project: Amortized explanation fits the per-frame budget of contribution 5 better than sampling methods; needs training of the explainer and still yields a heat map.
notes: Content from an abstract fragment on a repository page and from the survey arXiv 2509.01991; volume 12, pages 31047 to 31054 per that survey. Same first author as BSED (IEEE Access 2024).

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: Rethinking explainable AI: The gap between saliency-based explanation and user understanding for object detection models
key_idea: User study with tasks that measure understanding of an object detector at feature, instance and system level; showing the detector output helped, while adding saliency maps gave no further benefit.
method: Forward and counterfactual simulation tasks before and after training with or without saliency explanations; eye-movement analysis.
reported_result: Preprint abstract (SSRN): saliency explanations did not add understanding or direct attention to relevant features; output alone did not help users tell hits from misses or understand the system level.
relation_to_project: Strongest evidence found that heat maps alone may not help an operator (contribution 6); whether the cue-level explanations of the slides do better is untested.
notes: Abstract read from the SSRN preprint (10.2139/ssrn.5298798), which states the final article is published; the IJHCS listing snippet matches. A shorter CogSci 2024 paper by the same authors reports the same direction (eScholarship page seen).

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: ML-LOO: Detecting Adversarial Examples with Feature Attribution
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI 2020)
key_idea: Adversarial examples spread their feature attributions differently from clean inputs; thresholding a dispersion statistic of leave-one-out attribution maps, extended across layers, flags them.
method: Leave-one-out feature attribution; dispersion measures such as the interquartile range; multi-layer extension for mixed-confidence attacks.
data: Several real image data sets (abstract); CIFAR-10 with ResNet in a figure caption.
reported_result: AAAI abstract: better separation than compared detectors on popular attacks, transfer between attack methods, and competitive results when the attacker knows the detector; no numbers read.
relation_to_project: Shows that explanation statistics can themselves be the alarm signal on top of a frozen model; a citing paper calls leave-one-out attribution very costly for large inputs, against the latency goal of contribution 5.
notes: Classification only, digital perturbations. Cost remark from arXiv 2105.01959 (medical-data detection paper, not catalogued).

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: When Explainability Meets Adversarial Learning: Detecting Adversarial Examples using SHAP Signatures
key_idea: Uses SHAP values computed for internal layers of the protected network as a signature of each input and trains a separate classifier on these signatures to tell adversarial from benign inputs.
method: SHAP explanation signatures from hidden layers fed to a binary detector (description in citing papers).
data: CIFAR-10, named by a citing paper.
relation_to_project: Attribution-as-feature detection like ML-LOO; it yields a score, not an operator-facing reason, and SHAP computation per frame is a latency question for contribution 5.
notes: Abstract not read in this run (arXiv host stopped); content from two citing papers. A peer-reviewed version (IJCNN 2020, recalled from memory) is UNVERIFIED.

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: NeuroShield: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Adversarial Robustness
key_idea: Adds symbolic attribute heads (shape, colour, icon, category) to a traffic sign classifier and trains with semantic and logic losses that enforce class-implies-attribute rules, aiming at robustness and interpretable predictions.
method: Modified ResNet18 with shared features for class and attribute heads; soft implication rules from class-wise attribute dictionaries; adversarial training with FGSM or PGD.
data: GTSRB; FGSM and PGD at an L-infinity budget of 8/255.
reported_result: arXiv abstract: adversarial accuracy 18.1% and 17.35% above the matching adversarial-training baselines without loss of clean accuracy; ResNet18 trained for 10 epochs.
relation_to_project: Rule-based sign attributes as on slide 01: disagreement between predicted class and predicted shape or colour could serve as a readable alarm reason. Tested only on digital L-infinity attacks, not physical patches or light.
notes: Preprint, not peer reviewed; a Research Square version (2026) also exists. Using attribute disagreement as an alarm is our reading, not a claim of the paper.

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: Fooling Network Interpretation in Image Classification
venue: 2019 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
key_idea: Adversarial patches optimized to cause misclassification while suppressing Grad-CAM at the patch, so the interpretation no longer reveals the attack; doubles as a controlled test of interpretation reliability.
method: Patch optimization with an added loss on the Grad-CAM heat map at the patch location; transfer to occluding-patch interpretation tested.
data: ImageNet images (code example uses ILSVRC2012 validation images); VGG-19-BN in the paper figure.
reported_result: Abstract: the patches fool the prediction and change the interpretation; the effect tuned for Grad-CAM transfers to occluding-patch interpretation.
relation_to_project: Adaptive-attack threat to any alarm that relies on a heat map pointing at the disputed region (slide 01, SentiNet-style evidence); the evaluation of contribution 6 should include explanation-aware attacks.
notes: Classification only; detector-level versions not checked. arXiv 1812.02843 is the preprint.

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning in Adversarial Environments
venue: 2024 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
key_idea: Systematizes attacks on post-hoc explanation methods, defines a hierarchy of explanation-aware robustness notions, relates existing defenses to it and lists research gaps for explanations that resist manipulation.
method: Systematization of knowledge: threat models, attack scopes and types, robustness notions, defense taxonomy.
relation_to_project: Frame for testing whether the alarm explanation of contribution 6 survives an adversary who targets the explanation itself; the abstract states current explanation methods are not robust to manipulation.
notes: Pages 2441 to 2459 per the IEEE CSDL page. Same group: Disguising attacks with explanation-aware backdoors (IEEE S&P 2023), not catalogued.

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: Are explainable AI (XAI) evaluation strategies aligned? Comparing subjective, objective, and mathematical evaluation measures using saliency maps
key_idea: Preregistered user study comparing three saliency methods under subjective, objective and mathematical evaluation; the three families disagree, and mathematical metrics are not reliable proxies for user performance.
method: Between-subjects study with trust and satisfaction questionnaires, accuracy-estimation and prediction tasks, and fidelity, complexity, robustness and localization metrics.
data: Image classification task with LIME, Grad-CAM and guided backpropagation; 166 participants (abstract).
reported_result: arXiv abstract: no differences in trust or satisfaction; Grad-CAM improved user performance; mathematical metrics favoured guided backpropagation.
relation_to_project: Warns that contribution 6 cannot be shown by faithfulness metrics alone; an alarm explanation also needs a task-based user check, even a small one.
notes: Crossref lists issue year 2027 (online 2026); arXiv 2504.17023 (2025) is the preprint. Classification setting, not object detection.

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: ODExAI: A Comprehensive Object Detection Explainable AI Evaluation
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (book chapter)
key_idea: Evaluation framework that scores detector explanation methods on faithfulness, localization and complexity, including run time, so method choice can follow the task.
method: Quantitative metrics such as insertion, deletion, pointing game, energy-based pointing game and sparsity, plus run time, applied to several detector XAI methods.
data: YOLOX and Faster R-CNN on MS COCO and PASCAL VOC; Tesla T4 GPU (arXiv text).
reported_result: arXiv text: D-CLOSE most faithful; G-CAME best localization (PG 94.31%, EBPG 67.16% on YOLOX and COCO) and fastest at 0.43 s versus 70.12 s for D-CLOSE and 98.67 s for D-RISE.
relation_to_project: Cost side of question 1: sampling explanations take tens of seconds per image, CAM-style ones under a second, which bounds what an alarm explanation can use per frame (contribution 5).
notes: Results excerpt read in the arXiv 2504.19249 html (v1), abstract not read; numbers may differ in the published chapter. Crossref gives online 2025 and print 2026; book title not in the record.

category: X4-F2 Explanation methods for object detectors
title: BSED: Baseline Shapley-Based Explainable Detector
key_idea: Extends Baseline Shapley values to object detection so detector explanations satisfy the explainability axioms, with an approximation that keeps cost reasonable; model-agnostic, and explanations are used to correct detections.
method: Baseline Shapley attribution per detection target with a cost-reducing approximation; compared on energy-based pointing game, deletion, insertion and axiom metrics.
data: MS COCO and PASCAL VOC (arXiv results table).
reported_result: arXiv results table (COCO): insertion 0.667 for BSED with K=4 versus 0.636 for D-RISE and 0.496 for Grad-CAM; deletion 0.034 versus 0.035 and 0.142.
relation_to_project: Axiom-backed attribution and an example of explanations feeding back into detection decisions, close to using an explanation inside the alarm; cost per frame not read.
notes: Journal reference IEEE Access 12 (2024) 57959 to 57973 per the arXiv listing. Same first author as P2-P1313.

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: Human attention guided explainable artificial intelligence for computer vision models
key_idea: Uses human attention maps as an objective plausibility measure for detector explanations and learns to combine gradient and activation maps to match human attention, raising plausibility, faithfulness and trust for detectors.
method: FullGrad-CAM and FullGrad-CAM++ for object detection; HAG-XAI learns activation functions and smoothing kernels against human attention maps.
reported_result: Abstract: for object detection, HAG-XAI improved plausibility, faithfulness and user trust together and beat compared XAI methods; existing methods were less faithful than human attention maps.
relation_to_project: Driving-scene (BDD-100K) evidence on judging detector explanations against human attention; relevant to the operator-facing part of contribution 6.
notes: arXiv 2305.03601 is the preprint (seen in search results, not in the ledger). Overlapping authors with P2-P1314.

category: X4-F1 Explainable detection of adversarial inputs
title: WIP: From Detection to Explanation: Using LLMs for Adversarial Scenario Analysis in Vehicles
venue: 3rd USENIX Symposium on Vehicle Security and Privacy (VehicleSec 2025)
key_idea: Work in progress: structured scene descriptions plus the MUTCD traffic-control manual feed zero-shot chain-of-thought prompts so an LLM states whether an anomaly is a benign sensor error or an adversarial manipulation, and why.
method: Domain-specific language encoding of vehicle and scene data; MUTCD as knowledge base; zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting; explanations compared with references by ROUGE, BLEU and SBERT plus manual review.
reported_result: Abstract: larger models (Gemini named) reason better and often cite the relevant MUTCD sections; paper text gives SBERT up to 0.6915 for Gemini-1.5-pro.
relation_to_project: Text-form alarm explanation that separates benign errors from attacks (contribution 3 and the benign or abstain branch of the slides); it reasons over symbolic scene descriptions, not pixels, and one LLM call per alarm is far above the slide latency budget.
code_or_data: https://github.com/tigerseclab/VehicleSec25_LLM_Reasoning (stated in the paper, not opened) UNVERIFIED
notes: NEEDS_VERIFY: USENIX proceedings carry no Crossref DOI and no arXiv id was found; venue, pages 315 to 324 and authors read on the USENIX page through websearch. Work-in-progress paper; review process not checked. Related text-reasoning work seen, not catalogued: Hudson (arXiv 2409.14488) and an LMM sign-verification WIP (VehicleSec 2024).

category: X4-F3 Evaluation of explanations and operator-facing evidence
title: Explanations Help: Leveraging Human Capabilities to Detect Cyberattacks on Automated Vehicles
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2025)
key_idea: Online video study of whether in-vehicle displays help people detect attacks on infrastructure, perception and execution modules; alerts with explanations helped and softened false alarms, while bare alerts did worse than no display.
method: Online video survey comparing no display, Alert and Alert plus Explanations across three attack types and alert-attack alignment conditions; detection, trust, situation awareness and usability measured.
reported_result: Abstract: perception-module attacks were easiest to detect; execution-module attacks hardest, eased by Alert plus Explanations; participants were prone to false alarms, and explanation displays reduced their negative impact.
relation_to_project: Operator-facing evidence for contribution 6: under false alarms a bare alert did worse than no display, so the slide decision node should attach a short reason; the study used videos, not a live drive.
notes: Open access under CC BY 4.0 per the ACM page. Related, not catalogued: VehicleSec 2023 study of human drivers' situation awareness under physical-world attacks (10.14722/vehiclesec.2023.23002, Crossref record in the ledger) and a VehicleSec 2025 poster on explanations and takeover (preliminary results).
